title: policy-engine: support route-level experiment configs + precedence vs canaries/fallbacks
author: Jordan Lee
description: Summary: This PR extends the policy engine model to include route-level experiment definitions (A/B variants + allocation + eligibility) and codifies precedence rules with existing rollout primitives (canaries/model pinning) and fallback routing. Motivation: Console-first route experiments need a stable control-plane representation that can be evaluated quickly at request time, without changing gateway routing code paths for each new experiment feature. This PR adds the experiment config type, updates the policy compiler, and makes precedence explicit and testable so we don’t regress reliability guarantees (fallback) while enabling measurement (experiments). Precedence (high level): (1) Hard blocks/disable switches (project/route disabled, capacity blocks) (2) Explicit overrides (force_model / emergency routing override if present) (3) Experiment assignment (if an active experiment matches eligibility and is valid for the route) (4) Canary rollout policy (if configured for the route) (5) Default pinned model for the route (6) Fallback policy only applies after an upstream failure/guardrail trigger; fallback is not part of the initial selection unless we fail to select a viable primary target. Key behavior: Experiments select a primary target (variant) deterministically downstream; policy engine is responsible for emitting a normalized “experiment context” object (experiment_id, variant_ids, allocation, hash key semantics) and for ensuring that only one experiment is considered for a route at a time. Canary and experiment overlap is allowed only when the canary is scoped to a different route selector OR the experiment is explicitly marked higher priority; otherwise config validation fails with a clear error message. Data model changes: Adds ExperimentPolicy to policy schema v12 (backwards compatible). Adds route selector matching and eligibility constraints (tenant/project/region + optional header allowlist). Adds validation rules to prevent: duplicate variant ids, allocations not summing to 1.0, unsupported model compatibility (arch/context length mismatch) and ambiguous overlaps. Also adds a “policy_resolution_reason” enum to aid debugging and to support Console “why did this route go to X?” tooling. Testing: Adds unit tests for precedence matrix + validation. Adds integration-style tests for policy compilation with mixed configs (experiment + canary + fallback). Notes: This PR does not emit exposure logs; it only produces an experiment-aware routing decision context. Exposure emission is handled in gateway instrumentation (tracked separately). Checklist: [x] Backwards compatible schema bump + migrator tests [x] Validation errors are actionable (include route selector + conflicting policy ids) [x] Added golden tests for precedence ordering [x] Security review: ensure no PII in policy model; eligibility only supports allowlisted header keys (no free-form) [x] Perf: compilation overhead < 1ms for typical policy bundles; request-time evaluation unchanged (decision is precompiled). Release notes: Internal only (behind feature flag in Console); adds policy schema v12 with experiment policies and precedence semantics used by route-level A/B testing.
commits: policy schema v12: add ExperimentPolicy + RouteSelector constraints
compiler: compile experiments into resolved route policies
precedence: make selection order explicit; add resolution reason
validation: allocation sum, variant uniqueness, overlap detection
tests: precedence matrix + golden compilation snapshots
snippet: Precedence (compiler output): if (override) return override_target; if (experiment_match) return target_with_experiment_context; if (canary_match) return canary_target; return pinned_target; // fallback evaluated only on failure path
review_conversation: Ravi Menon: I’m concerned about “fallback only on failure path” wording. Today some routes effectively treat “no viable target” as a fallback trigger. Can you clarify what happens when a variant points to a model that isn’t available in a region? Jordan Lee: Good call. I updated compile_experiments() to filter targets by region availability at compile time (based on model catalog snapshot) and to fail validation if an active experiment would have zero viable targets for an allowed region. At runtime, if the selected target errors, fallback remains in the data-plane path as before. Mina Haddad: Can we make the experiment-vs-canary precedence configurable? Some customers will want canary to remain top-level. Jordan Lee: For v1 we should keep a single global order to reduce ambiguity. I added “priority” to the experiment policy but only as an internal knob; validation rejects values other than DEFAULT right now. We can expand once we have clearer product semantics. Ethan Park: Please add a resolution reason that is stable enough to expose in Console later (not tied to internal enum names). Jordan Lee: Added PolicyResolutionReason as a stringly enum in the compiled artifact (e.g., OVERRIDE, EXPERIMENT, CANARY, PINNED_MODEL). Tests updated. Chloe Martin: Validation errors need to be user-facing for Console. The overlap error currently references internal policy ids; can we include route selector and the human name field? Jordan Lee: Updated error formatting to include route_selector summary and display_name when present. Marcus Lin: Security: eligibility headers should be allowlisted; no raw header values should be stored/echoed. Also watch for project_id vs tenant_id confusion. Jordan Lee: Implemented header key allowlist (x-redwood-user-id, x-redwood-session-id) and ensured we only store keys, not values. Also added explicit naming in schema: tenant_id and project_id are separate fields, both optional, and validation enforces at least one scoping dimension. Ravi Menon: Looks good with the availability check. Approved. Mina Haddad: Approved once tests pass. Ethan Park: Approved. Marcus Lin: Approved (security notes addressed).
merge_outcome: Merged into main; schema v12 available behind feature flag (Console entitlement gating handled in follow-up PR).
